newsitem.title: USA: California mother puts her nagging on disc.
newsitem.headline: California mother puts her nagging on disc.

text.p: Giving new meaning to the phrase "sounding like a broken record," a mother who grew tired of nagging her son to tidy his room or pick up his toys decided to make a record of her commands and play it instead.
Rowena Starling, from Berkeley, near San Francisco, has made a compact disc of 23 of her most common instructions and is marketing it to other frustrated parents.

For years, Starling told Reuters, she would tell her son Grady, now 11, to pick up his toys or straighten up his room, but the commands often fell on deaf ears and she became "tired to death" of repeating them.
"I'd say, why don't I just record it and play it over instead of me saying it? It dawned on me to do exactly that," she said.

Using her own funds, she made a compact disc of the commands, repeated calmly but insistently for about 30 seconds each. They include instructions such as get up, make your bed, straighten your room, don't talk back. They often are accompanied by a reason for the request.
Starling recorded the disc, called "I'll say it again," under the name "Harper." She calls what she does on the record is "harping" rather than "nagging."

The divorced mother of one said she only plays the disc for her son "when I'm at the end of my rope," but that it works. "I put it down there and start to play it and he will move to do the chore because he doesn't want to hear the commands over and over," she said.
Starling, who is also a painter, is selling the disc for $11.95 and has sold "a couple of hundred" copies in the last few weeks. She donates a portion of each sale to schools.
